notes: The circuit and schematic images did not load, so the wiring follows the circuit text and the code comments. Hole positions are my own layout.

Step 1 was wrong in one respect: it had 5 jumper wires. I added wire6 (tp.12 to 14b.g) to carry 5V to the button's supply side. The button straddles the centre gap, so its two sides sit in the top and bottom halves, and no single rail reaches both. Everything else from step 1 is unchanged.
Sensor divider: photoresistor from the 5V rail to A0, with a 10k resistor from A0 to the GND rail. A0 reaches the breadboard through wire3.

Button: side 1 (top half) is the input side. Pin 2 comes in through wire4 and the 10k pull-down r2 goes to GND. Side 2 (bottom half) is fed from 5V through wire6, so pressing the button drives pin 2 HIGH.

LED: pin 9 goes through wire5 and the 220 ohm resistor r3 to the LED anode, and the cathode goes to the GND rail. The tutorial puts the 220 ohm resistor in series with the LED but doesn't say which side. I put it on the anode side.
Component legs go straight into the power-rail holes (tp.5, tn.8, tn.14, tn.24), so no extra wires are needed. The tutorial doesn't say whether it does this.
The code also drives the built-in LED on pin 13, which is on the Uno board, so there is no part or edge for it.
